gap: No result ChatGPT got gives a measured figure for how long the built-in memory lasts before loop recording starts overwriting. DashCamTalk's bench test filled the REDTIGER F77's 128 GB eMMC (114 GB usable) in about 4.1 hours of front and rear recording. DashCamTalk's bitrates for the 70mai M800 (29.4 + 10.1 Mbps) work out to about 7.2 hours on the same 128 GB, and for the DDPAI Z90 Master (42.1 + 30.1 + 17.8 Mbps) to about 1.6 hours on 64 GB.
standout_why: I compared against the cited rivals I could open. The carcody.com M500 review (26 Sep 2026) lists only 70mai's claims (up to 230 MB/s read and 150 MB/s write, 5 V 2 A) and has no measured hours, bitrate or transfer speed. The text of the cited manuals.plus M800 manual PDF couldn't be read, so I couldn't check whether it lists recording hours. The other cited pages wouldn't load: 70mai.store and ddpai.com returned HTTP 429, incartec.com had a certificate error, and shopredtiger.shop failed DNS lookup. None of them is a reviewer measurement. According to DashCamTalk, REDTIGER claims '8 hours recording for the 128GB version', and the bench test with both cameras recording got about half that. ChatGPT's answer lists eMMC capacities only and never says how many hours they hold.
decides: This supports ChatGPT's M800 pick for front and rear recording. At DashCamTalk's bitrates, the M800's 128 GB holds about 7.2 hours, while the F77 with the same 128 GB filled in a measured 4.1 hours because it records the rear at about 24 Mbps. The Z90 Master's 64 GB eMMC holds only about 1.6 hours across three 4K/3K channels, so its microSD slot (up to 512 GB) is a real need, not an optional extra. Copy speed is slow on both eMMC-only cameras: about 18.5 MB/s over USB-C on the M800 and 15.5 MB/s on the F77. That costs time when saving clips.
